speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are concerning for serious underlying pathology. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool characteristics regarding your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The weight loss and night sweats are quite significant; have you noticed any blood in your stool or black, tarry stools?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC shows leukocytosis and mild anemia, suggesting an inflammatory or proliferative process, but the lack of provided ESR data limits the inflammatory assessment. Have you experienced any unexplained fevers, and do you have any history of gastrointestinal symptoms like diarrhea, constipation, or early satiety?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of the supraclavicular node as "fixed" is highly concerning for malignancy rather than reactive lymphadenitis. Given your age and the "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss), do you have any history of smoking, alcohol use, or a family history of lymphoma or gastrointestinal cancer?

REQUEST TEST: LDH (Lactate Dehydrogenase).
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal CT scan.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) is Elevated. Abdominal CT Scan findings include massive enlargement of axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes, with splenomegaly detected and dullness noted over the left lower quadrant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma with splenic involvement.
